card.name: Words leading into FDA-approved tests
card.fires_on: Small words such as "an", "by", "using" and the hyphenated "-approved" just before "FDA-approved test" in patient-selection text for cancer drugs. Also weakly seen on a bracket after a lab instrument name.

modes.label: Before FDA-approved test
modes.description: The word "an" or "by" right before "FDA-approved/authorized test" when selecting patients by a mutation.
modes.example: Select patients for treatment with TAGRISSO based on the presence of a mutation as detected by<< an>> FDA-approved test.

modes.label: Inside FDA-approved
modes.description: The "-approved" part of "FDA-approved" in lines about tests for detecting mutations.
modes.example: Information on FDA<<-approved>> tests for the detection of BRAF V

modes.label: Instrument makers list
modes.description: An opening parenthesis after an analyzer model, before the manufacturer name.

card.plain: It fires on the small words that lead into "FDA-approved test" when a cancer drug label says patients are chosen by a mutation test.
